papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces InstructGPT and RLHF for aligning language models with human intent, showing how human feedback training shapes model responses including in morally-charged contexts.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces Constitutional AI (CAI) where models are trained using a set of principles rather than human labels, demonstrating how explicit value prompts during training shape model moral behavior.

papers.title: Whose Opinions Do Language Models Reflect?
papers.authors: Santurkar, S., Durmus, E., Ladhak, F., Lee, C., Liang, P., & Hashimoto, T.
papers.abstract_snippet: Shows that language model outputs systematically reflect certain demographic opinions over others, with prompting and persona effects revealing how prompt design influences expressed values.

papers.title: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates that LLMs can simulate diverse human survey responses through demographic prompting, but the fidelity of simulation depends heavily on prompt engineering and persona specification.

papers.title: Moral Foundations of Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Probes LLMs for moral foundations, showing that system prompts and role-playing instructions significantly shift expressed moral values, demonstrating the malleability of LLM moral profiles.

papers.title: RLHF: Whose Culture, Whose Values?
papers.abstract_snippet: Critically examines whose cultural values are embedded through RLHF training, arguing that alignment processes privilege particular cultural and moral perspectives over others.

papers.title: Helpful, harmless, honest? Sociotechnical limits of RLHF
papers.abstract_snippet: Analyzes the sociotechnical limitations of RLHF alignment, arguing that the helpful/harmless/honest framework embeds implicit moral assumptions that constrain how models handle ethical dilemmas.

papers.title: Decoding Human Preferences in Alignment: Inverse Constitutional AI
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes inverse Constitutional AI to decode the implicit human preferences embedded during alignment training, revealing hidden value assumptions in the alignment process.

papers.title: Constitution or Collapse? Exploring Constitutional AI with Llama
papers.abstract_snippet: Explores the effectiveness of Constitutional AI principles in open-source models, testing whether constitutional prompting reliably shapes moral behavior or leads to inconsistent outputs.

papers.title: Robustness of large language models in moral judgements
papers.abstract_snippet: Tests the robustness of LLM moral judgments under various prompting perturbations, finding that small changes in prompt wording can significantly alter moral judgment outputs.
